paper_metadata.title: A HYBRID QUANTUM WASSERSTEIN GAN WITH APPLICATIONS TO OPTION PRICING

summary: The paper presents a hybrid qWGAN for loading distributions into 5-qubit quantum states and then uses IQAE on a 7-qubit IBM device for option pricing. Quantitatively, the Wasserstein setup improves the loading benchmark from relative entropy 0.1858 to 0.0043 and Wasserstein distance 0.017387 to 0.001394, while the European call pricing example reports target/trained/estimated payoffs of 0.1618/0.1623/0.1661 with a 99% confidence interval of [0.1512, 0.1810].

experiments.description: Hybrid qWGAN training to load a lognormal distribution into a 5-qubit quantum generator, benchmarked against a BCE-based qGAN setup.

algorithm.variant: hybrid quantum Wasserstein GAN (quantum generator + classical discriminator)
algorithm.ansatz: TwoLocal circuit with RX/RY rotation layers and shifted-circular-alternating CX entanglement

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 5 qubits represent 2^5 = 32 discrete output states mapped to values 0.0 to 3.1 in steps of 0.1
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize Wasserstein-1 distance between generated and target discrete distributions
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: classical discriminator with linear output for Wasserstein setup; no explicit penalty terms reported

problem_instance.description: Load a discretized lognormal distribution representing stock prices at maturity

dataset_specification.description: Lognormal(mu = ln(1.1) - 0.25^2/2, sigma = 0.25), rounded to one decimal place; values mapped to 32-point grid from 0.0 to 3.1

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: sample 10000 points; round to one decimal; no scaling needed because max value is 3.1
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compare BCE vs Wasserstein setups after 2000 epochs using relative entropy and Wasserstein distance; select result with best relative entropy

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: generate and discretize lognormal training set; map to 32-point grid
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compute relative entropy and Wasserstein distance between generated and target distributions

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: oscillatory; Wasserstein setup more stable than BCE

speedup_claims.factor: O(poly(n)) loading vs O(2^n) prior state-preparation methods
speedup_claims.conditions: for loading arbitrary classical distributions into n qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity claim for the qGAN loading channel, not a wall-clock benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(poly(n)) for loading distributions with qGANs

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 5-qubit variational generator plus classical discriminator; 2000-epoch training on simulator; no end-to-end runtime advantage demonstrated
limiting_factors: No classical runtime baseline for the same loading task
Hybrid workflow depends on classical training and measurement sampling
No evidence of end-to-end quantum speedup

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the generator training is stated to be conducted on Qiskit's aer_simulator; the paper also reports final option pricing on real hardware separately, but this experiment is the distribution-loading benchmark.
num_variational_params inferred as 10 from 5 qubits and 2 layers with (l+1)n RY parameters described in the paper; the paper explicitly states 10 parameters for the generator.
num_shots inferred as 1024 from the paper's general statement that measurements are often taken with 1024 shots; no separate shot count is given for this benchmark.

The paper reports improved fit of the Wasserstein setup over BCE, with relative entropy 0.0043 vs 0.1858 and Wasserstein distance 0.001394 vs 0.017387, but this is not a quantum advantage claim in the Hoefler sense.

experiments.description: Hybrid qWGAN option-pricing pipeline for a European call option using the trained 5-qubit generator and Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation on real IBM hardware.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) used after hybrid qWGAN state preparation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: estimate option payoff with IQAE; no explicit stopping rule reported

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 5-qubit discretized distribution loaded into quantum state; 2 ancilla qubits used for payoff mapping and amplitude estimation
problem_formulation.objective_function: estimate E[max(ST-K,0)] via ancilla amplitude P(|1>)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: comparator circuit flips ancilla when ST > K; linear objective rotation maps payoff to amplitude

problem_instance.description: Pricing a European call option under a lognormal stock-price distribution with strike K=1.0

dataset_specification.description: same synthetic lognormal distribution as in exp_1; 5-qubit discretization

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compare target distribution payoff, trained distribution payoff, IQAE estimated value, and 99% confidence interval

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: train qWGAN on synthetic lognormal data; discretize distribution to 32 grid points; build comparator and payoff-rotation circuits
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: convert measured ancilla probability to option value; compute confidence interval

speedup_claims.conditions: for estimation accuracy epsilon; IQAE used instead of QPE
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states quadratic improvement in error scaling; the reported 20-minute runtime includes queue time on IBM hardware.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: quadratic improvement in error scaling over classical Monte Carlo via IQAE
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: about 20 minutes on ibm_nairobi including queue time

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 7-qubit IBM device with 2 ancilla qubits; IQAE used to estimate option payoff
limiting_factors: No classical baseline runtime for the full option-pricing pipeline
The claimed benefit is quadratic error scaling, not demonstrated wall-clock advantage
Hardware queue time and noise dominate practical execution
Distribution loading remains a major bottleneck

notes: The paper states that the evaluation on ibm_nairobi uses m = 2 ancilla qubits and that the device has 7 qubits available; total qubit count is therefore 7 for the full option-pricing circuit.
The paper does not report circuit depth, gate counts, or transpiled depth for the IQAE circuit.
num_shots inferred as 1024 from the paper's default shot count statement; the exact shot count for this run is not separately specified.
The paper reports a quadratic improvement in error scaling for IQAE, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over classical methods.
